During a validation site survey, you realize that the installers mounted some of the APs above the ceiling. They said that this was a request from the building architect due to aesthetics constraints. During the requirements gathering, you weren't advised about any aesthetics constraints from the main stakeholder of the project. What should you do in this case?
Remove all external antennas and use only the internal antennas to reduce multipath.
Advise the stakeholder that WLAN performance requirements will not be met and a new design process will be needed to meet the requirements.
Leave it as it is and allow automatic channel management to correct any issues.
Increase the output power on all APs by 6 dB immediately.
B

Mounting APs above the ceiling changes the propagation environment and adds attenuation not included in the design. Explain the performance impact to the stakeholder and revisit the design rather than simply increasing power.

What is the most suitable antenna option to be used when designing a WLAN infrastructure with APs mounted on a ceiling with a height of more than 20 feet and having all of the client stations used from the floor?
Patch
Dish
Low-gain dipole
Grid
A
A ceiling-mounted patch antenna directs more energy toward the floor area than a broad omnidirectional pattern, making it useful for high-ceiling deployments where clients are below the AP.
A wireless network with fewer APs at higher power levels to cover a large area is said to be which of the following?
Capacity based
Coverage based
Destined for failure
Ideal for roaming
B
A coverage-based WLAN uses fewer APs at higher transmit power to cover a larger area. It prioritizes broad reach over the smaller cells and greater reuse used in capacity-based designs.
What metric implements the simplest algorithm and lowest accuracy in networks requiring locations?
Angle of Arrival (AoA)
Time of Arrival (ToA)
Time Difference of Arrival (TDoA)
Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI)
D
RSSI is a simple signal-strength metric used to estimate distance for location, but multipath and environmental variation make its location accuracy relatively low.
A bandpass filter has a maximum in-band loss of 1.5 dB, ripple of 0.4 dB, and a return loss of 15 dB. What is the minimum in-band loss?
1.1 dB
1.5 dB
1.9 dB
A
Minimum passband loss equals maximum insertion loss minus the specified ripple: 1.5 dB − 0.4 dB = 1.1 dB.
The installation crew for your WLAN project wants to install a few APs to locations nearby the ones specified in the RF design document. What next step should occur?
Confirm the mounting hardware.
Choose a different AP model.
Update the documentation.
Consult the RF designer.
D
The RF designer owns the technical rationale for AP placement. Consult them before moving APs so the change can be assessed against coverage, capacity, and interference requirements.
Looking at a client radio specification sheet that states Receive Sensitivity of −82 dBm @ 18 Mbps would mean:
It would need to hear a signal <−82 dBm in order to use the 24 Mbps PHY rate.
It is only capable of transmitting at 18 Mbps PHY rates at −82 dBm.
It must hear a signal >−82 dBm in order to demodulate the 18 Mbps PHY rate.
It must hear a signal <−82 dBm in order to demodulate the 18 Mbps PHY rate.
D

The supplied key states that the signal must be below −82 dBm, but receive sensitivity normally means the minimum usable signal is approximately −82 dBm or stronger (less negative). Verify this wording/key before relying on it.
What term refers to the security practice of obfuscating actual data from unintended receivers as the data crosses the transmission medium?
Confidentiality
Authentication
Integrity
Accounting
Nonrepudiation
A
Confidentiality protects the contents of data from unauthorized disclosure while it traverses the wireless medium.
When troubleshooting coverage issues for a wireless network as it appears to new client associations, you should perform which type of survey?
Active survey
Passive survey
A survey is not necessary.
Predictive survey
B
A passive survey listens to beacons and measures RF coverage without associating to the WLAN. It is appropriate for checking whether new clients can discover adequate signal in the affected area.

In a convention center, you have received complaints about the WLAN infrastructure. At this moment, there are only two APs in one auditorium. After analyzing the situation, you determined that there are more client devices that the infrastructure was designed for. There are only two APs to support more than 300 devices using the Wi-Fi at the same time. What should you do to make the Wi-Fi work as expected?
Redesign the entire WLAN
Upgrade the Ethernet connections to MultiGig
Quickly add more APs
Turn up the output power on the APs so that they can handle more clients
A
When user density exceeds the original design assumptions, redesign capacity for the actual client count and application demand rather than simply turning up AP power.
What are some advantages of designing guest access with all guest users tunneled directly into the DMZ?
Minimizes configuration requirements for segmentation and filtering of guest traffic across internal LAN
Enhances performance of web proxy servers in the DMZ for guest Internet traffic
Allows a single SSID with different authentication/encryption models to be used for all WLAN services for corporate users and guests
The border firewall configuration will not require any additional rules to pass guest traffic to the DMZ controller
A
D
Designing guest access with all guest users tunneled directly into the DMZ has two main advantages:
What are three potential benefits when an organization lets their employees bring their own device onto the company s network"?
Enhanced productivity Decreased costs and Increased satisfaction
Enhanced productivity Increased costs, and Decreased satisfaction
Enhanced productivity. Increased costs, and Increased satisfaction
increased security Enhanced productivity, and Decreased attack surface
A
BYOD can improve employee productivity and satisfaction while reducing the organization's device acquisition costs, provided security and support policies are addressed.
If a 24-port switch has a PoE budget of 740 W, how many IEEE 802.3at devices can certainly be powered on by it?
D

The supplied answer key selects 18 devices. Check the AP's actual IEEE 802.3at power draw and the switch's per-port and total PoE limits; the class maximum and the switch's stated budget determine the guaranteed count.

When designing a new WLAN infrastructure you also need to be aware of now the network is physically deployed and now the network is logically configured What are two documents that are helpful In this case?
Bill of Materials and Blueprints
Hold Harmless and Network Diagrams
Network Diagrams and Network Closet Locations
Blueprints and Network Closet Locations
C
Network diagrams document logical/physical connectivity, while network closet locations identify where equipment and cabling infrastructure are physically installed.
Which one of the following options would you consider a well-designed WLAN infrastructure when measuring RSSI Notse floor and SNR in a required area?
Low RSSI, Low Noise Floor Low SNR
High RSSI, Low Noise Floor High SNR
High RSSI, High Noise Floor Low SNR
Low RSSI, High Noise Floor Low SNR
B
SNR is the difference between the received signal level and the noise floor. To meet a target SNR, add the required SNR to the measured noise floor.

You have been asked to design a WLAN for an organization. They will be replacing an existing WLAN Currently each AP operates 8 SSIDs on each radio What will you communicate with the organization so that they understand the need to reduce the number of SSIDs?
implementing loo many SSIDs results in decreased data rates
Implementing loo many SSIDs results in decreased throughput
Implementing loo many SSIDs increases ACl in every scenario
Implementing too many SSIDs reduces SNR in every scenario
B
Each SSID adds beacon and management-frame overhead. Excessive SSIDs consume airtime and can reduce capacity, even when user data traffic is low.
What is an advantage of centralized data forwarding?
It reduces delay for user traffic
It increases the encryption strength for user traffic
It increases the signal strength for wireless client devices
It allows for centralized filtering of wireless traffic
D
Centralized forwarding sends client traffic through the controller, where centralized policies such as filtering and inspection can be applied consistently.
If you choose to recommend dynamic channel assignment for the APs in your WLAN design what action should you also recommend'?
Ensure that the output power of all APs is set to the maximum allowed in the regulatory domain
Ensure that the output power of an APs is set to the minimum available in the system interface
Replace all antennas with panel antennas instead of omnidirectional antennas
Configure the settings used by the dynamic channel assignment algorithm optimally for your design
D
Dynamic channel assignment should be tuned to the design: define the eligible channel set, channel widths, power ranges, and interference/coverage thresholds instead of relying blindly on defaults.

An AP vendor being considered for a WLAN deployment suggests that their 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz dualband APs use software defined radios What unique capability does this indicate in comparison to non-software defined radios?
At least one radio can be configured for either 2.4 GHz or 5 GHz operations
The radios can have their SSIDs configured through software
Software is used to configure the encryption settings
Software is used to configure the entire WLAN profile
A
A software-defined radio can change its operating band or radio role through software configuration, subject to the AP's supported hardware capabilities.
Even when a full pre-design site survey is not performed, what is always recommended to be performed within the deployment areas?
A spectrum analysis walkthrough
An AP-on-a-stick survey of 37% of the facility as this amount provides all of the statistical information required for good design
A scan in the 5 GHz band looking for common IoT interferers
A scan in the Sub-1 GHz bands to determine if sideband interference will impact 2.4 GHz operations
A
A spectrum-analysis walkthrough identifies non-Wi-Fi RF interferers before AP placement and channel planning. It is a useful baseline even when a full site survey is not performed.
